items.title: Bob Lovett Interview, 1949-04-01
items.q: No, I think I was mainly trying to emulate the sound of Johnny Dodds. ... I never met him or I never saw him or heard him in person.

ctx.x: G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Now you mentioned Jolly Roll and Louie. Do you remember any of the other recording leaders?
G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Well, some of those small groups were Johnny Dodds. Generally the New Orleans groups we were mainly impressed with.

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. By that time they had become also called the South Side groups. They had made many of these recordings in Chicago. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yeah. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. They were the New Orleans men. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Now, many of the early Chicagoans had listened to the original Dixieland Jazz Band, then later to the New Orleans Rhythm Kings. At any time do you remember those coming into your observation?
